answer: A plume of cheap fake identities collapses when every agent must stake a refundable deposit before joining a market. A single whisper of fraud triggers a random peer audit: auditors verify the agent's work history and signed task receipts, and a failed audit slashes the stake and burns the identity. Honest agents recover their deposit plus a fee, so creating many identities is expensive while staying honest is cheap. Like a jetty that lets only real boats dock, the stake-and-audit gate makes Sybil attacks cost more than they can earn.
